original_question: For an open dynamical system with a hole H ⊂ Ω, survival probability P(t), escape rate γ = - lim_{t→∞} (1/t) ln P(t), and natural invariant measure ν on the repeller, for which classes of maps and flows does the escape-rate formula γ = ∑_{i:λ_i>0} λ_i - h_KS remain valid, where the sum runs over positive Lyapunov exponents and h_KS is the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy computed with respect to ν?
target_in_paper: Problem 11.1 in Section 11.3, whose exact formulation is "How general is the escape rate formula, Eq. (11.6)?", stated immediately after the definitions of Ω_t, P(t), the conditionally invariant measure μ_∞, the repeller measure ν, and Eq. (11.6). ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target very closely: it uses the open-system setting with a hole H⊂Ω, the survival probability P(t), the escape rate γ, the natural invariant measure ν on the repeller, and the precise escape-rate identity γ=∑_{i:λ_i>0}λ_i−h_KS with Lyapunov exponents and KS entropy taken with respect to ν. It also correctly asks about validity across maps and flows, which is exactly where the paper says further development is needed. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
missing_details: The paper defines the survivor set Ω_t={x∈Ω: Φ^s(x)∉H for all s∈(0,t]} and then sets P(t)=μ_0(Ω_t) for an initial probability measure μ_0; your draft omits μ_0 and the definition of Ω_t. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

It matters that t denotes either discrete time for maps or continuous time for flows; for billiards the default is continuous time unless stated otherwise. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The hole H is not arbitrary in the setup: it may lie on the boundary or in the interior, may have several connected components, and is assumed piecewise smooth, with codimension 1 for flows and full dimension for maps. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The formula is posed only after introducing the renormalized survivor measures μ_t(A)=μ_0(Φ^{-t}(A)∩Ω_t)/μ_0(Ω_t) and a limiting conditionally invariant measure μ_∞; these are part of the paper’s hidden assumptions behind ν. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The repeller measure ν is defined explicitly by ν(A)=lim_{t→∞}e^{γt}μ_∞(A∩Ω_t); your draft names ν but does not state this defining limit. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The paper frames the question as one of generality beyond the settings already understood—especially beyond strongly or uniformly hyperbolic systems—and explicitly points to further development for maps without uniform hyperbolicity and for flows. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

For flows versus maps, the paper stresses that conditionally invariant measures for the flow Φ and the collision map F need not be equivalent, so the flow case is not a trivial corollary of the map case. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The surrounding discussion also notes that proofs often replace the sum of positive Lyapunov exponents by the unstable Jacobian; in two-dimensional billiards there is at most one positive Lyapunov exponent. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
refined_question: Let Φ^t:Ω→Ω be an open dynamical system, with t∈ℤ for maps or t∈ℝ for flows, and let H⊂Ω be a piecewise smooth hole (of the same dimension as Ω for maps and codimension 1 for flows). Define the survivor set Ω_t={x∈Ω: Φ^s(x)∉H for all s∈(0,t]} and, for an initial probability measure μ_0, the survival probability P(t)=μ_0(Ω_t). Assume the escape rate γ=−lim_{t→∞}(1/t)ln P(t) exists, the renormalized survivor measures μ_t(A)=μ_0(Φ^{-t}(A)∩Ω_t)/μ_0(Ω_t) converge to a conditionally invariant measure μ_∞, and the natural invariant measure on the repeller is ν(A)=lim_{t→∞}e^{γt}μ_∞(A∩Ω_t). Under what dynamical hypotheses—especially beyond the strongly or uniformly hyperbolic cases already understood, and in particular for maps without uniform hyperbolicity and for flows—does the escape-rate formula γ=∑_{i:λ_i>0}λ_i−h_KS(ν) hold, where the Lyapunov exponents λ_i and the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy h_KS are computed with respect to ν? ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
justification: This draft is clearly aimed at Section 11.3’s Problem 11.1 rather than a neighboring problem. The exact paper formulation is intentionally terse, but the immediately preceding text supplies the necessary notation and assumptions: survivor sets, escape rate, conditional invariance, the definition of ν on the repeller, and the statement that Eq. (11.6) generalizes Pesin’s formula. The author then emphasizes that known results are mainly in strongly hyperbolic settings and that the unresolved direction is extension to maps without uniform hyperbolicity and to flows. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
